geology_notes: Churchill Resources holds the Foxtrot past-producing antimony mine (Frost Cove / Black Raven property) in central Newfoundland, and has expanded its district land position through the March 2026 Golden Baie option (39,925 ha, TSXV-approved March 27, 2026) and a Black Raven LOI. Confirmed geological highlights from accessible disclosures: (1) FC25-27: 13.00% Sb over 0.57m at Frost Cove — validated after the May 2026 data-correction release that downgraded the broader initial assay dataset; (2) a second new polymetallic system at southern Frost Cove / Black Raven yielding 7.25% Sb over 1.98m; (3) a 20-vein Au-Ag-Mo-Pb-Zn swarm at Pomley Cove Pond with surface channel results including 17.3 g/t Au and 130 g/t Ag; (4) zinc grab samples at Black Raven reaching 5.25%, 11.03%, and 12.11% Zn with associated Au, Ag, and Pb. Nine 2026 drill holes completed circa July 13 remain without confirmed public assay release as of July 31 — eighteen days since the 'imminent' assay announcement; two targeted news-index searches conducted today found no results headline. The August 2023 NI 43-101 technical report remains the most recent on file; the extraction yielded no compliant resource estimate in the first 60 pages. All five resource/reserve fields are null per extraction. Score of 3 reflects confirmed high-grade multi-commodity mineralisation across a consolidated NL property package, constrained by absence of a compliant resource estimate and eighteen days of post-drill silence on pending 2026 assay results.

catalyst_notes: Macro catalyst: China's September 2024 antimony export controls restricted supply from the dominant global producer and have sustained Western-government urgency for domestic and allied critical mineral supply chains. Antimony is named in Canada's Critical Minerals Strategy and on the US Defense Production Act designated minerals list, making Foxtrot a credible candidate for NRCan/provincial grant support and strategic partnership interest. This macro tailwind remains durable as of July 31, 2026. Company-specific catalyst (adverse): CRI shares fell approximately 20% on July 15, 2026, closing near C$0.04. The specific trigger remains unconfirmed despite searches and prior fetch attempts — no explanatory headline has been indexed. The timing — two days after the nine 2026 drill holes were reported completed circa July 13 — is notable. As of July 31, the 2026 assay batch is now eighteen days past the 'imminent' announcement with no results headline indexed. Score of 2 maintained: macro tailwind is structurally intact; the CEO transition during an assay-pending window, the unexplained July 15 stock decline, and eighteen days of assay silence together constitute accumulating near-term negative signals.
